answers.answer: In the 3-player case, the tied lead gets no coin; the unique last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, while the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Census: tied lead gives no coin; unique last pays, except the 2-player last player never pays.

answers.answer: You may draw fewer than six. You cannot draw more than the two free Market spaces allow. Undrawn Followers already on your Market remain there between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Followers: draw any number up to allowance, limited by free Market spaces; unused Market Followers remain and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds, but cannot execute it until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall needs only one space). You may save a fully activated action for a later round. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology remains.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Planning and Actions: gradual filling, activation condition, saved activation; ordinary action Followers return to bag and Technology stays.

answers.answer: Starting with the Start Player, players go clockwise repeatedly, taking one activated action or passing. Passing ends your participation for that Action Phase, so you cannot act again; your unused activation and its Followers remain on the board for a future round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Actions: clockwise one action or pass; passing ends participation; unused activations keep Followers on board.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances your Farmers Track one space, and gives you the good depicted at that space.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Farm House.

answers.answer: Village lets you recruit one of Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader into your bag and advance that profession’s track. Boatman gives the depicted coins (or a Citizen to the first player at the last space); Craftsman gives a Technology tile; Trader gives a Place Tile, with category I only on the first advance and I or II on later advances.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment section.

answers.answer: The newly acquired Technology cannot help execute another action this round; it is used only after you pass. Your first placed Technology must replace a Farmer. Later Technology can replace any profession except Monk; never place more than one Technology at one Place or any Technology at a Place requiring only one Follower. Technology stays in place and cannot be moved.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment, Craftsman; Technology section.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance allows category I only; every later advance allows category I or II. Players may inspect the Place Tile stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment, Trader; Setup, Place Tiles.

answers.answer: University puts a Scholar in your bag, advances the Scholars Track one space, and gives its depicted Development Points. Castle puts a Knight in your bag and advances the Knights Track one space. Monastery puts a Monk in your bag with no extra track reward. The fourth Knight leaves draw allowance at 7 (no increase at that step); the first player to that space takes its Citizen. Once a character track is at its last space, you cannot take that corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: Actions table; Castle rewards; Character-track limits.

answers.answer: A Monk may replace a Knight on an ordinary action. A Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. A Monk also cannot substitute for the exact profession required by a Beneficial Deed.
answers.evidence: Monks; Technology; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Ship moves your Merchant along one Waterway to an adjacent town; Wagon moves along one Road to an adjacent town. Each action may take at most one good from that connection, even if two lie there. Empty connections are legal and yield no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods section.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant currently is. A town with any player’s station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Guildhall; Building section.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gives 1 Development Point (move one space on the Development Track). Moving onto or past a coin space collects its depicted coins; the first player onto/past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching or passing a Development Status space immediately changes your Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Scriptorium; Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: Town Hall can be activated with one or two eligible Followers; you may send one or both in one action. Your four marked starting Followers cannot enter Town Hall. Send each to a free Beneficial Deed space matching its exact profession. Each placement gives its depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; Canalization gives a choice of 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The Follower stays permanently on the Deeds board. Whoever fills a Deed’s last empty space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds section.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment during the Action Phase (Phase 5), even though the tile is revealed in Phase 1; it is not deferred to the Event phase. Other events resolve in Phase 6. Round 1 opens with Pilgrimage because that tile is placed on top of the prepared Hour Glass stack.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Hour Glass and Event; Setup, Hour Glass stack.

answers.answer: Only grain, cheese, or wine qualifies as food; wool and brocade do not. If you cannot pay food, you pay 5 coins instead. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you cannot pay the 5 coins, torture applies for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Events, Harvest.

answers.answer: If Plague draws a neutral Scholar, return it to its game-board supply, where it becomes recruitable again; do not move its track marker back. If it draws your marked starting Trader, keep it, lose no Follower, and do not redraw.
answers.evidence: Events, Plague.

answers.answer: Pay the one available coin, then replace each of the two missing coins with one eligible item, in any mix: a built or unbuilt Trading Station; a random eligible Follower drawn only from your bag (marked starting Followers are returned and redrawn until an eligible neutral one is drawn); one Development Point moved left without moving onto or past a coin space; one Goods Tile, Place Tile, or Technology tile. Items surrendered are removed from the game.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy).

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods Tile, even if another part would still give a reward. It becomes available again when its required tile is available, subject to the usual requirements. If the common coin supply is insufficient, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies.

answers.answer: If two players tie for most built stations, nobody takes the bonus Citizen; it goes only to a unique leader. Each grain/cheese/wine/wool/brocade is worth 1/2/3/4/5 points. Coins are 1 point each. Built stations plus collected Citizens are multiplied by final Development Status. Tied scores go to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, they share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: Each player receives a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Place the four starting Followers on your Market, Merchant in Orléans, one marker on the first space of each of the six Character Tracks and the Development Track, and keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. The youngest player takes the Start Player token.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 2 and final sentence.

answers.answer: In a 4-player game, sort neutral Followers by profession into their board buildings, Technology into its supply, and coins nearby; put 13 Citizens on their marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II. Shuffle goods face down and deal one face up on every eligible Road/Waterway goods space; sort remaining goods face up into the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 1, 3, and 5; 4-player goods instruction.

answers.answer: For 3 players, remove 2 neutral each of Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders; 3 each of Knights, Scholars, and Monks; and 6 random goods, leaving spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players, remove 4 neutral each of Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders; 6 each of Knights, Scholars, and Monks; and 12 random goods, leaving spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table and preceding sentence.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table, required Followers column.

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table, required Followers column.

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall takes one or two eligible Followers; the four marked starting Followers cannot enter it.
answers.evidence: Actions table and Town Hall/Beneficial Deeds section.

answers.answer: Yes. For each of two draws you decline, you may instead move one Follower from an Action Space back to your Market. This is the permitted way to recover assigned Followers; you may not move one directly from one Action Space to another.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Followers.

answers.answer: Yes. You may inspect your bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Followers.

answers.answer: The seven phases are Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. At the end of each round pass Start Player left. Planning is simultaneous; announce completion and plan in clockwise order from Start Player if order matters. Event payments and other order-sensitive resolution proceed clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to the common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, seven phases.

answers.answer: Do not score immediately: finish the entire round in which the 18th tile is drawn, including its event; score afterward.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: The player uniquely ahead on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin; the number of Farmer tiles in bags does not affect Census.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Census.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Events, Income; Scoring, Status.

answers.answer: Eight goods means two complete groups of three, so pay 2 coins; goods types do not change the count. If you lack the coins, torture applies for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Events, Taxes.

answers.answer: You receive 4 coins, one per built Trading Station; the six unbuilt stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Events, Trading Day; Building.

answers.answer: Hayrick costs Farmer and takes 1 grain from the Goods Market; Cheese Factory costs Farmer + Farmer and takes 1 cheese from the Goods Market; Winery costs Farmer + Trader and takes 1 wine from the Goods Market; Wool Manufacturer costs Boatman + Trader and takes 1 wool from the Goods Market; Tailor Shop costs Scholar + Trader and takes 1 brocade from the Goods Market. A goods-producing Place cannot be used if that good is absent from the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table and following goods availability rule.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman, gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk, gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman, gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar, gain 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins, advancing one Development space per coin; paying two advances two spaces. Zero and four coins are not allowed.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Pharmacy.

answers.answer: Cellar: Monk + Scholar, gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar, gain 1 coin per built Trading Station. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar, gain coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight. It moves along one Road to an adjacent town and collects one good if available.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Horse Wagon.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile. Your first Technology cannot be placed there because it must replace a Farmer. A later Technology may replace either Laboratory space if no Technology is already there and usual constraints are met.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Laboratory.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires a Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces; none can go on the Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Farmer to your bag.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Bathhouse.

answers.answer: Place the one drawn Follower that can legally go on an allowed Action Space. Return the other two drawn Followers and the activating Bathhouse Farmer to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Farmer to your bag.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Bathhouse: if only one or none can legally be placed, do so and return all other draws; standard rule returns activating Follower.

answers.answer: It may be executed later this round on a later action turn, provided you have not passed. Actions can be chosen in any order, and passing ends your participation.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Actions: choose actions’ order freely; passing ends participation.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 you return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Sacristy.

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5. Sacristy protection is used in Phase 6, after the Action Phase, so it does not change the recruitment restriction.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Hour Glass and Event; Sacristy Phase 6 protection.

answers.answer: Herb Garden allows Boatmen to replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not permit replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Herb Garden.

answers.answer: School allows Scholars to replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. School requires no activation. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, School.

answers.answer: No. Beneficial Deeds require exact depicted professions; Place substitutions cannot replace them. Gunpowder Tower retains that exact-type rule.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds; Gunpowder Tower summary.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3, place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. During Planning, move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, in Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in a single action. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent, and Deed spaces still require exact types.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table, Gunpowder Tower.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two tied furthest behind pay nothing.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Census: tied last place pays nothing.

answers.answer: The uniquely most-stationed player receives the set-aside Citizen after the entire 18th round, including its event, and before scoring. It counts as a collected Citizen for final scoring.
answers.evidence: Setup; Scoring / Victory Conditions: unique most takes set-aside Citizen before scoring; collected Citizens count in station/Citizen formula.

answers.answer: At setup, remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then place Pilgrimage on top. In Phase 1, the Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup, Hour Glass stack; Turn Structure, Hour Glass.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions table.

answers.answer: Development Status starts at 1 and initial Knight-track draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2.

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered goods, Followers, stations, Places, and Technology are removed from the game, not returned to supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy).

answers.answer: You may choose the execution order freely; neither printed order nor order filled is required.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Actions: choose your actions’ order freely.

answers.answer: Its passive ability is available immediately, including during the Action Phase in which the Place is acquired.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment, Trader.

answers.answer: You may send just one or both. Town Hall needs only one of its two spaces for activation, and in one action sends one or both.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Planning; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: You may take one good from the connection; the summary does not say it is mandatory. Thus the move may be completed without taking the available good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: “You may take one good” from the connection.

answers.answer: You may send the second in a later action turn in the same Action Phase before passing; the FAQ explicitly allows Town Hall’s two Followers to be sent in separate action turns.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings, Town Hall in separate action turns.
